scope: Highlight overlay start, reload, control, bridge admission, capture and clear; saved history and Data/Scrape handoffs checked for preservation

supported: The pending session is published before saved-history lookup; completion rechecks both object identity and the active pageKey after each awaited start stage (src/lib/highlights/session.ts:12-42).

Injection and control messages address the exact Chrome document and carry sessionId; the content overlay rejects later control messages with a different token (src/lib/highlights/control.ts:14-77; src/lib/highlights/highlighter.ts:440-466).

The bridge admits state, capture and clear only from the represented tab, top frame, document, URL and session token; capture rechecks the token after organization and bearer waits, before insert (src/hooks/use-highlight-bridge.ts:22-27,65-89; src/lib/highlights/queries.ts:166-216).

The view presents the represented session on its initiating page and a Stop there control from another page; URL/domain saved-history filtering and Data/Scrape handoff logic remain separate (src/features/highlights/HighlightView.tsx:82-108,139-181,194-214).
A_scoped_outcome.clear_semantics: Clear is admitted on receipt and rechecked inside the user's confirmed action before clearHighlightsForUrl starts (src/hooks/use-highlight-bridge.ts:86-113). The helper then selects and soft-deletes saved IDs for the captured URL (src/lib/highlights/queries.ts:293-318). A subsequent session change during the database read does not, by itself, prove a wrong-target or unauthorized deletion: saved URL history is deliberately shared across documents, and the confirmed action was valid when it began. Cancellation after that point is an optional product policy, not an established defect in this scope.
